diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner instance as soon as its launch configuration and instance profile exist, but the instance role's docker-machine permissions may not yet be attached. Ensure the group waits for this policy attachment before launching instances.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group may launch the runner agent before its IAM role policy attachment granting docker-machine permissions is installed. The group should wait for the attachment so the agent can use those permissions as soon as it starts.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The runner's instance role needs the cache policy available to its instances; the Auto Scaling group can launch before this attachment is complete. Ensure the attachment precedes instance launch.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The runner instance role needs the cache policy attachment before the runner can use the configured S3 cache. Ensure the attachment is in place before the Auto Scaling group launches an instance.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
When enabled, the runner's user data relies on SSM access from the instance role, but the Auto Scaling group can launch before this policy attachment is complete. Ensure the attachment precedes instance launch.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
When token management is enabled, runner user data uses SSM to manage the registration token. The Auto Scaling group should wait for this role-policy attachment so the instance has the required SSM permissions when it starts.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
When enabled, runner instances need the service-linked-role permissions attached to their instance role before they start using AWS services; the Auto Scaling group does not wait for this attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
When service-linked-role creation is enabled, the runner agent needs this policy attachment before it starts using its instance role; otherwise its initial operations can race the attachment and fail to create service-linked roles.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
With CloudWatch logging enabled, runner instances need the inline logging policy before startup; the Auto Scaling group can launch before that policy is attached to the instance role.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Auto Scaling group can launch the runner agent before its inline CloudWatch Logs role policy is installed. Because logging is enabled by default and the instance user data configures logging, wait for this policy before creating the group.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
When CloudWatch logging is enabled, the runner's startup logging configuration uses the environment log group, but the Auto Scaling group can launch instances before that log group exists. Make the group creation precede instance launch.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The runner's user-data logging configuration may start before the managed CloudWatch log group exists. Ensure the group is created before the Auto Scaling group launches the runner instance.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The user-data script manages the runner registration token in SSM, but the autoscaling group can launch its instance before the parameter resource is created. This can race the startup script against Terraform's initial parameter write; make the group wait for the parameter to exist.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The runner's user-data flow manages the registration token in this SSM parameter. Waiting for the parameter to exist avoids the instance attempting to write it before Terraform has created it.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The runner agent's user-data script manages the value of aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token (the parameter is created by Terraform with a placeholder value and the instance writes the real token into it). The autoscaling group boots the agent instance but expresses no dependency on the SSM parameter; if the instance starts before the parameter exists, the user-data script creates it and Terraform's own creation of the parameter subsequently fails. The parameter must be created before the autoscaling group launches instances.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The autoscaling group boots the runner agent instance whose user-data script writes the GitLab runner token into SSM (aws ssm put-parameter on local.secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key). aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token (with lifecycle ignore_changes on value) must exist before that script runs, otherwise the script creates the parameter itself and Terraform's aws_ssm_parameter create later fails with "parameter already exists". No attribute reference connects the ASG/launch configuration to the SSM parameter, so this ordering is not captured by the graph.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance sets policy_arn via local.bucket_policy, which resolves to module.cache.policy_arn when cache_bucket.create is true. No direct dependency on the cache module is expressed, so the attachment could be created before the cache bucket policy exists.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance attaches the cache-bucket policy via local.bucket_policy, which resolves to module.cache.policy_arn (the S3 bucket policy created by module.cache), but the graph shows no dependency on module.runner:module.cache. The cache bucket and its policy must exist before the policy can be attached to the runner instance role. Inlining the local's expression as a direct reference to module.cache establishes the ordering as a data dependency.

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
data.template_file.runners renders the runner config with vars.bucket_name sourced from local.bucket_name, which resolves to module.cache.bucket when cache_bucket.create is true. The rendered config (which ends up in the runner agent's user-data) references the cache bucket, so the data source should depend on the cache module being created; no such dependency is expressed.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
data.template_file.runners renders the runner config.toml with the S3 cache bucket name taken from local.bucket_name, which resolves to module.cache.bucket, but the graph shows no dependency on module.runner:module.cache. The cache bucket must exist (and its name be known) before the runner configuration referencing it is rendered and baked into the runner agent's user data. Inlining the local's expression as a direct reference to module.cache establishes the ordering as a data dependency.
